# Producers, agents and events

Read from the code: every public name below, its signature and its docstring. Import `igni_service` — defined in `igni_service.agent_wire`, `igni_service.agents`, `igni_service.events`.

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`Agent`](#agent) | One producer's agent — a person's or an app's — in one organisation. |
| [`Attachment`](#attachment) | A file to send with an item: any type igni's composer takes, at most 5 MiB. |
| [`Chat`](#chat) | The chat of one thread in one producer's igni. |
| [`EventAccepted`](#eventaccepted) | igni stored the event. `expires_at` is the time igni kept. |
| [`ItemStatus`](#itemstatus) | What became of an item: `GET /v1/service-events/{event_id}`. |
| [`Producer`](#producer) | Whose agent the event is for: a person or an app of the organisation. |

## Agent

```python
class Agent
Agent(org_id: str, producer: Producer, wire: AgentWire)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org_id` | `str` | required | The organisation the agent's items go into, as the id ``igni.host()`` was given. |
| `producer` | `Producer` | required | Whose igni every item goes to: the person or the app the agent is for. |
| `wire` | `AgentWire` | required | The wire the items go over: the calls to igni server. |

One producer's agent — a person's or an app's — in one organisation.

### Agent.producer

```python
@property
producer: Producer
```

Whose igni this agent is: the person or app every item goes to.

### Agent.send_message()

```python
async def send_message(
    text: str,
    *,
    attachments: list[Attachment] | None = None,
    thread: str | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    start_run: bool = True,
    event_key: str | None = None,
    expires_at: datetime | None = None,
) -> EventAccepted
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `str` | required | The message's words, as the agent reads them. |
| `attachments` | `list[Attachment] \| None` | `None` | The files to send with it: each is uploaded to igni first, and the message names it by its id. |
| `thread` | `str \| None` | `None` | The thread the message belongs to: the first message of a thread opens its chat, and every later one goes there. Without one the message goes to this extension's own chat. |
| `title` | `str \| None` | `None` | The chat's title, for the message that opens its thread's. |
| `start_run` | `bool` | `True` | Whether the message starts a run in the chat, or waits for the run already going. |
| `event_key` | `str \| None` | `None` | The key that makes a retry exact: igni stores one item per key and producer, so a retry after a lost reply is answered with the item already stored. |
| `expires_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | When igni stops waiting to deliver it: igni keeps an item for at most 14 days. |

Post `text` as this extension's message: it starts a run, or waits for the run going.

`start_run=False` waits for the chat's next run instead. `title`
names the chat if this message opens its thread's. Needs
`service.messages` (and `service.attachments`, `service.chats`
for files and a thread).

### Agent.send_event()

```python
async def send_event(
    type: str,
    payload: dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    event_key: str | None = None,
    expires_at: datetime | None = None,
) -> EventAccepted
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `str` | required | The extension's own word for what happened, as its handler names it: ``claim.created``. |
| `payload` | `dict[str, object] \| None` | `None` | The event's data, as the handler reads it: at most 65536 bytes as JSON. |
| `event_key` | `str \| None` | `None` | The key that makes a retry exact: igni stores one item per key and producer, so a retry after a lost reply is answered with the item already stored. |
| `expires_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | When igni stops waiting to deliver it: igni keeps an item for at most 14 days. |

Hand this extension an event. igni posts nothing for it: the extension's handler acts.

One no handler took reads `not_handled` (`status`). Needs no grant.

Open a chat titled `title` — for `thread`, or a thread of its own — optionally with a first message.

### Agent.chat()

```python
def chat(thread: str) -> Chat
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|

### Agent.status()

```python
async def status(event_id: str) -> ItemStatus
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | `str` | required | The item's id, as ``EventAccepted.event_id`` gave it. |

Where an item igni accepted stands, as igni holds it now.

`state` is one of:

- `pending` — stored; the producer's igni has not taken it yet.
- `delivered` — a message posted, or an event a handler took.
- `not_handled` — an event no handler took: no handler for its
  type, no running extension, or the handler raised;
  `not_handled_reason` says which.
- `expired` — not taken before `expires_at`.
- `dropped` — the producer no longer has the extension;
  `dropped_reason` says why.
- `failed` — the platform gave up; `failed_reason` says why.

Raises `EventRefused` for a 4xx (an unknown `event_id`, say) and
`IgniUnavailable` otherwise.

| `text` | `str \| None` | `None` | The item's words: the message's text, or the chat's first message. |
| `attachments` | `list[Attachment] \| None` | `None` | The files to send with the item: each is uploaded to igni first, and the item names it by its id. |
| `thread` | `str \| None` | `None` | The chat thread the item belongs to: the first item of a thread opens its chat, and every later one goes there. |
| `title` | `str \| None` | `None` | The chat's title, for the item that opens its thread's. |
| `start_run` | `bool` | `True` | Whether the item starts a run in the chat, or waits for the run already going. |
| `action` | `ChatAction \| None` | `None` | What an ``action`` item does to its thread's chat: show a view, rename it, or cancel the run working in it. |
| `event_key` | `str \| None` | `None` | The key that makes a retry exact: igni stores one item per key and producer, so a retry after a lost reply is answered with the item already stored. |
| `expires_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | When igni stops waiting to deliver it: igni keeps an item for at most 14 days. |

Any item: the methods above and `Chat`'s are this, spelled for one kind.

## Attachment

```python
class Attachment(BaseModel)
Attachment(
    *,
    filename: Annotated[str, MinLen(min_length=1), MaxLen(max_length=200)],
    content_type: str = 'application/octet-stream',
    data: Annotated[bytes, MinLen(min_length=1), MaxLen(max_length=5242880)],
)
```

A file to send with an item: any type igni's composer takes, at most 5 MiB.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filename` | `str` | required | The file's name, as people see it in the chat (1-200 characters). |
| `content_type` | `str` | `'application/octet-stream'` | Its media type. |
| `data` | `bytes` | required | Its bytes: at least one, at most 5 MiB. |

## EventAccepted

```python
class EventAccepted(BaseModel)
EventAccepted(
    *,
    event_id: str,
    expires_at: datetime.datetime | None = None,
    duplicate: bool = False,
)
```

igni stored the event. `expires_at` is the time igni kept.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | `str` | required | The item's id: pass it to `Agent.status`. |
| `expires_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | When igni stops trying to deliver it: what was asked, or igni's 14-day limit. |
| `duplicate` | `bool` | `False` | True when `event_key` matched an event already stored. |

## ItemStatus

```python
class ItemStatus(BaseModel)
ItemStatus(
    *,
    event_id: str,
    producer: Producer,
    kind: Literal['event', 'message', 'chat', 'action'] = 'event',
    type: str,
    thread: str | None = None,
    event_key: str | None = None,
    state: Literal['pending', 'delivered', 'not_handled', 'expired', 'dropped', 'failed'],
    dropped_reason: str | None = None,
    failed_reason: str | None = None,
    not_handled_reason: str | None = None,
    created_at: datetime,
    expires_at: datetime.datetime | None = None,
    delivered_at: datetime.datetime | None = None,
    updated_at: datetime,
)
```

What became of an item: `GET /v1/service-events/{event_id}`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | `str` | required | The item's id, as `EventAccepted.event_id` gave it. |
| `producer` | `Producer` | required | Whose igni the item was for. |
| `kind` | `ItemKind` | `'event'` | `event`, `message`, `chat` or `action`. |
| `type` | `str` | required | An event's type; for the other kinds, the kind igni recorded. |
| `thread` | `str \| None` | `None` | The chat thread the item belongs to, if any. |
| `event_key` | `str \| None` | `None` | The key the service sent it with, if any. |
| `state` | `ItemState` | required | Where it stands: `pending`, `delivered`, `not_handled`, `expired`, `dropped` or `failed` (`Agent.status` says what each means). |
| `dropped_reason` | `str \| None` | `None` | Why it was dropped, when `state` is `dropped`. |
| `failed_reason` | `str \| None` | `None` | Why the platform gave up, when `state` is `failed`. |
| `not_handled_reason` | `str \| None` | `None` | An event no handler took: why. |
| `created_at` | `datetime` | required | When igni stored it. |
| `expires_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | When it stops waiting to be taken. |
| `delivered_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | When the producer's igni took it, once it has. |
| `updated_at` | `datetime` | required | When its state last changed. |
